title: Metals sector weathers Middle East shock as aluminium deficit cut to 1 million tonnes, but copper surplus signals fragile stability
gist: Wood Mackenzie's 2026 mid-year review argues the Middle East conflict inflicted far less damage on metals than feared — the aluminium deficit was revised down from an expected 2.5-3 million tonnes to roughly 900,000 tonnes (the headline rounds this to 1 million) and copper still moves into surplus — but the real risk is lagged: depleting inventories, deferred investment, half of global sulphur supply disrupted, and cost pressure that has not yet surfaced in the numbers.

insights.claim: The 2026 global aluminium supply deficit caused by the Middle East conflict has been revised down to approximately 900,000 tonnes from an initial expectation of 2.5 to 3 million tonnes.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A deficit two-thirds smaller than feared removes much of the conflict premium priced into aluminium; positioning built on a 3Mt shortfall needs unwinding.
insights.quote: At the height of the conflict, the disruption was expected to generate a supply deficit of between 2.5 and 3 million tonnes. The revised expectation is approximately 900,000 tonnes.
insights.locator: The clearest evidence sits in aluminium

insights.claim: The article's own body figure of a 900 thousand tonne aluminium deficit is smaller than the '1 million tonnes' cited in its headline, so the rounded headline number overstates the revised shortfall.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Use 900kt, not 1Mt, when modelling the balance — the 100kt gap is the difference between a headline and the forecast.
insights.locator: News Release / Wood Mackenzie Mid-Year Review

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie characterises a 900 thousand tonne aluminium deficit and a slight copper surplus as uncomfortable figures that are merely less bad than the alternative, not signs of a healthy market.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Relief rallies on 'better than feared' metals data may be mistaking a smaller wound for recovery.
insights.quote: A 900 thousand tonne aluminium deficit and slight copper surplus are hardly comfortable figures. They are just not as uncomfortable as they might have been.
insights.locator: "The sector has so far absorbed a significant shock"

themes.theme: Sulphur chokepoint into copper and nickel

insights.claim: The Middle East conflict has disrupted half of global sulphur supply, and China's restrictions on sulphuric acid shipments compound that pressure on copper and nickel production, including in the DRC and Australia.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Sulphuric acid is the hidden input constraint on leach-based copper and nickel output — watch DRC and Australian producers for acid-driven guidance cuts.
insights.quote: The conflict has disrupted half of global sulphur supply, and China’s restrictions on sulphuric acid shipments have compounded the pressure on copper and nickel production.
insights.locator: The indirect effects are proving harder to contain

insights.claim: The indirect, input-chain effects of the conflict are proving harder to contain than the direct supply disruption to metals output itself.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Map second-order reagent and feedstock exposure (acid, sulphur, energy) rather than first-order mine or smelter outages when sizing conflict risk.
insights.locator: The indirect effects are proving harder to contain

themes.theme: Copper surplus and tariff-driven trade imbalance

insights.claim: Copper is expected to move into surplus in 2026, yet tariff-related inflows into the United States are creating trade imbalances that continue to support higher prices.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A surplus market with firm prices means the price signal is trade-policy artefact, not scarcity — US-domestic copper spreads are the trade, not outright length.
insights.quote: Copper is expected to be in surplus this year, with trade imbalances driven by tariff-related US inflows continuing to support higher prices.
insights.locator: The indirect effects are proving harder to contain

insights.claim: Approximately 32% of global direct reduced iron production was affected by the Middle East conflict, though DRI is a small share of overall global steel output.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A headline-grabbing 32% DRI hit is largely immaterial to global steel balances — discount it, but watch DRI-dependent EAF producers specifically.
insights.quote: Approximately 32% of global direct reduced iron production was also affected, though this remains a small share of overall global steel output.
insights.locator: The clearest evidence sits in aluminium

insights.claim: Global steel demand is faltering in the near term, independent of the conflict's supply-side effects.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Steel is a demand story, not a supply story, in 2026 — conflict headlines should not be read as bullish for steel margins.
insights.locator: The indirect effects are proving harder to contain

insights.claim: Lithium has passed through the conflict largely unscathed because existing oversupply and offtake concentrated in China insulate it from Middle East disruption.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Lithium offers no geopolitical-premium optionality; its price path stays governed by the oversupply and Chinese offtake cycle.
insights.quote: Lithium has continued through the disruption largely unscathed, backed by existing oversupply and offtake concentrated in China.
insights.locator: The indirect effects are proving harder to contain

themes.theme: Resilience is real but lagged and costly

insights.claim: Supply chain resilience built through COVID-19 and repeated trade and tariff shocks cushioned the metals sector because contingency plans were activated rather than built from scratch.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Prior-crisis muscle memory is now a real and under-modelled shock absorber — default disruption models likely overstate damage from the next event too.
insights.quote: Contingency plans were activated rather than built from scratch.
insights.locator: Supply chain resilience built through the COVID-19 period

insights.claim: The damage not yet visible in metals data is inventories depleting, cost pressures building slowly, investment decisions deferred, and demand reorienting away from China.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: These four are the leading indicators to track; each shows up in prices and capex with a lag of quarters, not weeks.
insights.quote: The concern now is what the numbers do not yet fully show: inventories depleting, cost pressures building slowly, investment decisions deferred, and demand reorienting away from China.
insights.locator: "The sector has so far absorbed a significant shock"

insights.claim: Trade frictions and the conflict are slowly exerting upward pressure on inflation while weighing on global growth and commodity demand, meaning resilience is being paid for rather than obtained free.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The macro cost of resilience is stagflationary at the margin — supportive of nominal commodity prices but hostile to volume growth.
insights.locator: Supply chain resilience built through the COVID-19 period

insights.claim: The US Federal Reserve has held rates steady on inflation concerns despite significant external pressure to cut.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A Fed on hold against political pressure keeps real rates restrictive for commodity-financing and capex decisions through 2026.
insights.quote: The US Federal Reserve has held rates steady in the face of inflation concerns despite significant external pressure to cut.
insights.locator: Supply chain resilience built through the COVID-19 period

insights.claim: The US mid-term elections are identified as the next major policy and market milestone for 2026, with the unforecast Middle East conflict raising their importance.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Position for a policy-inflection event around the mid-terms — tariff and electrification trajectories both hinge on it.
insights.quote: This compounds the importance of the US mid-term elections as the next major policy and market milestone for 2026.
insights.locator: Wood Mackenzie forecast a turbulent, fragmented world for 2026

insights.claim: The United States maintained tariffs through a range of mechanisms despite a court ruling against them.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Legal challenges are not a reliable off-ramp for tariff exposure — assume policy persistence when modelling US metal import spreads.
insights.quote: The United States maintained tariffs through a range of mechanisms despite a court ruling.

insights.claim: China's 15th Five-Year Plan shifted the country's emphasis towards advanced manufacturing, part of a 2026 outlook framed as 'two hemispheres, one turbulent economy.'
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Chinese metal demand mix tilts toward higher-value manufacturing inputs rather than construction-led bulk volumes.

insights.claim: Faltering oil and gas shipments pushed electrification discussions to 'fever pitch,' reframing the debate from reshoring jobs via trade barriers to building regional capability against geopolitical volatility.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The bull case for grid, power and electrification equipment is now national-security framed, which is more durable to fund than climate framing.
insights.quote: discussions around electrification reached, in the report's own words, "fever pitch,"
insights.locator: The conflict has also sharpened a domestic resilience debate

insights.claim: Whether electrification momentum survives a potential recession is explicitly left as an open question by Wood Mackenzie.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Treat the electrification bid as procyclical and vulnerable — a growth scare could stall order books faster than policy support offsets it.
insights.quote: Whether that momentum survives a potential recession remains an open question.
insights.locator: The conflict has also sharpened a domestic resilience debate

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie frames the outlook with two scenarios: 'Summer settlement,' testing whether apparent resilience is a lagged response before supply gaps hit downstream industries, and 'Extended Disruption,' modelling commodity outcomes under sustained conflict.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A usable binary for scenario-weighting metals books: the key discriminator is whether downstream industries report input gaps in H2.
insights.quote: "Summer settlement" examines whether apparent resilience reflects a lagged response before supply chain gaps reach downstream industries
